previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, COPD, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and chest tightness over five days, following a recent hospitalization for a similar episode. The flare was attributed to acute on chronic systolic heart failure, likely triggered by dietary indiscretion involving high sodium intake. He was treated with intravenous furosemide, transitioned back to oral torsemide, and received supportive care including antibiotics and steroids for presumed infection and COPD exacerbation. His symptoms improved, with resolution of pulmonary edema on imaging, stabilization of renal function, and correction of hyperkalemia. Blood glucose levels normalized after discontinuation of steroids. He was discharged home on his baseline medications with education on low-sodium diet and weight monitoring.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ M with multiple medical problems including CHF 
(EF ___, COPD, pulmonary fibrosis who p/w 2 days of nausea, 
vomiting, diarrhea with increased dyspnea and syncopal episode, 
found to have DVT of RLE.  

ACUTE ISSUES

# ACUTE ON CHRONIC SYSTOLIC CHF 
 Pt's JVD, ___ edema, & overall clinical picture including 
orthopnea, PND, and cough when supine all suggested CHF 
exacerbation. This was likely due to the fact that the patient 
has not been digesting his medications due to nausea and 
vomiting. Patient also has a component ___ on CKD which may 
be ___ CHF exaerbation as well. EKG unchanged from prior, and 
cardiac enzymes showed Tn 0.08 at baseline from last admission. 
The patient underwent diuresis with lasix with improvement in 
dyspnea. He was then transitioned back to his home Torsemide, 
and on day of discharge, his oxygen saturation was back to 
baseline on RA. 

# ___ ON CKD: 
Recent baseline creatinine appeared to be around 1.6. Creatinine 
on admission was 1.8 which may represent mild cardiorenal 
syndrome vs volume depletion due to n/v/d (although much less 
likely given pt appeared overloaded on exam). The patient was 
diuresed with downtrending Cr, and on day of discharge his Cr. 
was 1.7.

# SYNCOPAL EPISODE: 
The patient presented after a syncopal episode, most likely due 
to volume depletion given recent N/V/D. Pt endorses decreased PO 
intake, and feeling lightheaded. No bowel or bladder 
incontinence during witnessed syncopal episode. During 
admission, pt was eating and tolerating POs currently without 
further syncopal episodes. 

# RLE DVT
B/l ___ showed small deep vein thrombosis in one of the right 
deep peroneal veins. Pt was started on warfarin with heparin 
bridge. He was discharged with Lovenox and received teaching 
regarding proper administration of Lovenox. 

# Left Ankle Pain
Patient experienced sudden left ankle pain overnight. No hx of 
recent trauma. Patient states that similar swelling occurs 
intermittently at home. On exam the following morning, the 
patient denied current pain. He remained stable with tramadol 
and flexeril for pain and muscle spasms. 

 # NAUSEA, VOMITING, DIARRHEA: 
Patient presented with N/V/D, consistent with norovirus. No 
recent antibiotics to suggest C. Diff. No WBC count to suggest 
bacterial infection. Patient remained afebrile during admission, 
and was tolerating POs without nausea or vomiting on day of 
discharge. 

# CHEST PAIN
The patient had an episode of chest pain during admission. His 
EKG was unchanged from prior and cardiac enzymes not concerning. 
His chest pain resolved without further episodes. 
 
# TROPONINEMIA: Troponin 0.08 on admission which is within 
baseline given CKD. No chest pain or EKG changes. EKG this 
admission shows ST depression in lateral leads unchanged from 
prior. Enzymes cycled x3 and were stable. 

CHRONIC ISSUES
 
# COPD: 
The patient did not have active wheezing on exam and remained 
stable with nebulizers PRN.

# DM2:
The patient has a diagnosis of diabetes. He remained stable on a 
decreased insulin regimen from his home regimen due to concern 
for possible decreased PO intake given N/V. He also received an 
ISS. 

# ANXIETY:
The patient has a history of anxiety and remained stable on his 
home benzodiazepine regimen.
